summary: Self-service role elevation request returns 403 for DataHub UI and CLI after passkey SSO enforcement
description:
Issue summary: Multiple developers are unable to complete a self-service 'Request Access' flow for the internal DataHub tool. The UI returns a 403 on the final approval step and CLI token exchange for temporary elevated sessions fails with '403 Forbidden: insufficient permissions'. Impact: Blocks developer access to debug pipelines and runbook data; affects at least 6 engineers across two teams. Not a tenant-wide outage but prevents on-call rotations for Data team.

Observed behavior: After initiating an elevation request from Console -> DataHub -> Request Access, the frontend shows a 403 and the request fails to create a temporary role session. When using the CLI helper (rw-access request --role data-admin) the device opens the browser for SSO, completes Okta auth (passkey), and then the CLI prints 'Error: 403 insufficient permissions' after the token exchange.

Expected behavior: Self-service elevation should complete and issue a short-lived session credential per the standard runbook.

Relevant context: This started after last week's passkey-only SSO enforcement rollout (IDP policy change). Affected users appear to be using recently-provisioned device passkeys. The DataHub app is configured to accept Okta assertions and map groups to temporary roles via identity-proxy and RBAC service.

Impact window: First reports 2026-03-09 08:00 PST; reproducible as of 2026-03-10.
steps_to_reproduce: Login to Console (prod-us-west) as a developer with a passkey-enabled Okta account.
Navigate to DataHub -> Request Access -> select 'data-admin' role -> click Request.
Complete the Okta passkey flow when prompted.
Observe UI final screen shows 403 and request fails. Check browser network inspector for 403 response from /api/v1/elevations.
Alternatively run CLI: rw-access request --role data-admin and follow SSO. After redirect back to CLI, observe '403 insufficient permissions' during token exchange.
logs: identity-proxy ERROR 2026-03-10T15:02:21Z request_id=abc123 route=/elevations token_exchange failed status=403 msg=Missing claim 'auth_level'
rbac-service WARN 2026-03-10T15:02:21Z lookup user=svc-user-123 groups=[data-read] matched_roles=[]
console-frontend 2026-03-10T15:02:21Z POST /api/v1/elevations 403 122ms "{\"error\":\"forbidden\",\"detail\":\"user missing required auth claim\"}"
investigation_notes: 03-10 15:10: Confirmed 403 path originates in identity-proxy after Okta assertion is validated and before RBAC evaluation.
03-10 15:24: Pulled Okta assertion for affected user (okta-assertion-id=okta-789). Assertion missing 'auth_level' and 'amr' fields when login completed via passkey only.
03-10 16:00: Control test using password + MFA (non-passkey) returned an assertion that included auth_level='legacy' and amr=['pwd','mfa'], and elevation flow succeeded.
03-10 16:30: Checked last week's IDP policy rollout notes: passkey-only authentication profile was enabled org-wide on 2026-03-08. No identity-proxy changes were deployed in that window.
03-11 09:40: Reproduced on staging with synthetic passkey account; confirmed identity-proxy rejects assertions lacking 'auth_level' because RBAC rules require mapping based on auth_level >= '2'.
hypothesis: Passkey-only logins currently produce Okta assertions that do not include the 'auth_level' claim (or include a different AMR set). Identity-proxy's strict claim validation path treats missing auth_level as insufficient assurance and returns 403 before role mapping.
A recent Okta profile mapping change for passkey enforcement inadvertently dropped auth_level claim for newer device registrations.
actions_taken: 03-10 17:00: Escalated to Identity team and opened a Parked investigation in #identity-support with assertion sample and logs.
03-10 18:15: Temporary workaround documented: instruct affected users to sign in using password+MFA (if available) to complete elevation. Communicated to Data Pager and support channel.
03-11 10:05: Identity team confirmed they can reproduce in Okta sandbox and are preparing a mapping fix for auth_level claim.

03-12 09:00: Rolled a short-lived feature flag in identity-proxy to relax strict auth_level requirement for elevation flows in DataHub while patch is prepared (flag: allow_missing_auth_level_for_elevations=true).
comments: Aisha Khan (2026-03-10): Initial report from Data team. Provided example user ids and reproduction steps. Marking P2 since workaround exists but disrupts rotations.
Miguel Torres (2026-03-10): I can reproduce locally. Pulling Okta assertion now. Tentatively assigning to identity oncall.
Priya Singh - identity-oncall (2026-03-11): Confirmed missing claim behavior in Okta sandbox. Root cause likely mapping config. Creating internal Okta ticket ID OKTA-5792.
Miguel Torres (2026-03-12): Deployed identity-proxy feature flag to relax claim check in prod-us-west. Monitoring for successful elevations. Noted that we should revert once Okta mapping fix is live.
Data Team Lead - Jordan Lee (2026-03-12): Confirmed at least 4 engineers were able to elevate after the temporary flag. We'll keep monitoring for any policy/regression.
Miguel Torres (2026-03-12): Next steps: coordinate with IdP to patch mapping and then remove the temporary relax flag. Add a unit test for assertion -> role mapping to catch missing claims.
resolution_notes: Workaround applied: identity-proxy relax flag allowed affected users to complete elevation. Identity team is deploying Okta mapping fix (auth_level claim) and will follow with post-deploy validation. After Okta fix, revert relax flag and run test matrix for passkey and non-passkey flows.
next_steps: Identity team to push Okta mapping change to include 'auth_level' for passkey authentications (target 2026-03-13).
SRE/Identity to validate production assertion samples and run elevation flow smoke tests across auth methods post-deploy.
Remove temporary allow_missing_auth_level_for_elevations flag once Okta mapping fix validated.
Add automated CI check in identity-proxy to assert presence or safe defaulting for auth-related claims in elevation flows.
Update runbook entry to include guidance for passkey-only edge cases and add a troubleshooting snippet for missing claims.
